group-2023-jia-reading-a.overview: 一篇曼谷美食指南类应用文，逐一介绍曼谷五家值得一去的餐厅（Nahm、Issaya Siamese Club、Bo. lan、Gaggan），每家给出主厨、菜式风格、地位排名与就餐氛围等信息，属于典型的高考阅读 A 篇广告/指南文体。

discourseStructure.summary: 总—分结构：先用引言点出曼谷是美食爱好者的天堂、餐饮选择丰富，再按小标题分段逐家介绍各餐厅的特色。

paragraphs.summary: 全文大标题：在曼谷哪里吃。
paragraphs.function: 标题，点明文章主题为曼谷餐厅推荐。

paragraphs.summary: 引言：曼谷是美食爱好者向往之地，餐饮选择多到看似无穷，并引出下面的推荐；段末给出第一家餐厅小标题 Nahm。
paragraphs.function: 总起段，交代写作背景与全文框架。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍 Nahm：泰式精致料理，是唯一跻身全球 50 佳餐厅前十的泰餐厅；主厨 David Thompson 曾凭同名伦敦泰餐厅获米其林星，2010 年在大都会酒店开设此分店；段末引出 Issaya Siamese Club。
paragraphs.function: 分述段，介绍 Nahm 餐厅及其主厨。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍 Issaya Siamese Club：国际知名泰国主厨 Ian Kittichai 的首家旗舰店，菜单将传统泰餐与现代烹饪手法结合；段末引出 Bo. lan。
paragraphs.function: 分述段，介绍 Issaya Siamese Club 餐厅。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍 Bo. lan：2009 年开业后名声渐起，提供难寻的泰式菜肴，忠于泰餐本源又有独特创新，适合烛光晚餐或工作会餐，并为特别饥饿者提供大份套餐；段末引出 Gaggan。
paragraphs.function: 分述段，介绍 Bo. lan 餐厅及其套餐与氛围。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍 Gaggan：在亚洲 50 佳餐厅榜单上位列第一的前卫印度餐厅，最佳座位正对厨房，可见主厨 Gaggan 及员工现场烹饪，堪称最佳的烹饪剧场。
paragraphs.function: 分述段，介绍 Gaggan 餐厅及其开放式厨房特色。

group-2023-jia-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇人物报道，讲述26岁的Terri Bolton热爱并擅长DIY（自己动手），其技能源自已故的祖父、建筑工人Derek Lloyd；文章还引出一项新研究，说明DIY正日益流行且由女性引领潮流。

discourseStructure.summary: 由人物切入（擅长DIY）→ 追溯技能来源（祖父教导）→ 说明DIY在租房生活中的实际用处 → 引用研究数据展望DIY趋势，点出女性引领潮流。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍Terri Bolton擅长DIY，能自己搭架子、组装家具，从不花钱请人做自己能做的活。
paragraphs.function: 开篇点题，树立人物形象，引出DIY主题。

paragraphs.summary: Terri将DIY技能归功于已故祖父、建筑工Derek Lloyd；她六岁起便在假期跟随祖父干活，每天得到5英镑零花钱，并曾深度参与祖父建房。
paragraphs.function: 追溯人物技能来源，说明成长经历与情感纽带。

paragraphs.summary: 如今Terri在伦敦西南租房，她说DIY帮她在租期结束时避免被扣押金——她会补好墙洞、重新粉刷房间以免被收费。
paragraphs.function: 说明DIY技能在日常租房生活中的实际益处。

paragraphs.summary: 引用新研究：数百万人计划在夏季动手做DIY项目，人均花费约823英镑，多数人为提升居家舒适度，部分人为增值房产；研究显示如今是女性在引领这股潮流。
paragraphs.function: 由个人转向群体，用研究数据展望DIY趋势，呼应并升华主题。

group-2023-jia-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇书评，作者讲述自己少年时因一本哲学入门书爱上哲学，大学时期热情被浇灭，后来 Eric Weiner 的《The Socrates Express》重新唤起了他对哲学的热爱，并向读者推荐这本书。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按时间与逻辑推进：先回忆少年时与哲学的结缘，再写大学时热情的熄灭，转而引出重燃热爱的关键书籍，随后用两段具体评析该书的写法与价值，最后总评并发出阅读邀请。

paragraphs.summary: 作者约13岁时叔叔送他一本《苏菲的世界》，整个夏天沉浸其中，被带入哲学世界。
paragraphs.function: 引入：交代作者初识哲学的契机。

paragraphs.summary: 这份热爱持续到上大学，自以为比作者更懂哲学家并急于讲解的人浇灭了他的热情。
paragraphs.function: 转折：说明对哲学的热爱如何被消磨。

paragraphs.summary: Eric Weiner 的《The Socrates Express》重新唤起作者对哲学的热爱，它是一份体验哲学的邀请而非讲解。
paragraphs.function: 引出全文评析的核心书籍。

paragraphs.summary: Weiner 以列车旅途场景开篇，把每位哲学家的思想放在能帮我们做得更好的某件事的背景中，让读者学会运用哲学改善生活。
paragraphs.function: 评析该书的结构与主旨：教人用哲学改善生活。

paragraphs.summary: Weiner 用幽默让哲学思考变得有趣，并通过解读哲学家的思想、加入自己的诠释而融入其中。
paragraphs.function: 进一步评析该书的写作风格与作者的参与方式。

paragraphs.summary: 该书表面简单却引人深入思考欲望、孤独与衰老，作者发出明确邀请并鼓励读者抽时间一读。
paragraphs.function: 总评并发出阅读邀请，收束全文。

group-2023-jia-reading-d.overview: 本文是一篇说明文，介绍灰熊（grizzly bears）在美国的处境与种群恢复历程：人们对它既敬畏又恐惧；它一度因猎杀濒临灭绝，1975 年被列入《濒危物种法》后受到法律保护，种群逐步恢复；如今数量回升又引发是否撤销保护的争议；最后说明只要人们采取预防措施，便能与灰熊和平共处。

discourseStructure.summary: 文章先写美国人对灰熊既敬畏又恐惧的矛盾心理，并点出它是黄石公园游客最想见到的动物；接着指出灰熊正重新占据其历史栖息地、越来越多被人类目击；随后回顾灰熊从数量众多到因猎杀濒危、并于 1975 年被列入《濒危物种法》的历史；再讲述其恢复成功后两次试图被“摘牌”却因保护组织诉讼而被推翻；最后说明只要清除食物与诱物、采取电围栏等预防措施，人们就能与灰熊和平共处。

paragraphs.summary: 灰熊体型庞大，在美国人心中占据矛盾的位置——既被敬畏又令人恐惧；它也是涌入黄石公园的世界各地游客最想见到的动物。
paragraphs.function: 引入话题：呈现美国人对灰熊既敬畏又恐惧的矛盾心理。

paragraphs.summary: 熊类生物学家 Chris Servheen 指出灰熊正重新占据其昔日活动范围，随着它们扩展到一个多世纪未见其踪迹的地区，越来越多地被人类目击。
paragraphs.function: 承接发展：说明灰熊种群正在扩张、与人类接触增多。

paragraphs.summary: 欧洲人到来时美国西部灰熊众多，约五万头以上；经过定居者数百年残酷而持续的猎杀，到 20 世纪 70 年代初仅剩 600 至 800 头，栖息地仅存 2%，1975 年灰熊被列入《濒危物种法》。
paragraphs.function: 回顾历史：交代灰熊从繁盛到濒危并被立法保护的过程。

paragraphs.summary: 如今美国约有 2000 多头灰熊，恢复非常成功，鱼类与野生动物管理局两度试图将其“摘牌”以放松保护、允许狩猎，但都因保护组织提起诉讼而被推翻，灰熊仍受保护。
paragraphs.function: 呈现争议：说明灰熊恢复后是否撤销保护的拉锯。

paragraphs.summary: 若不采取预防措施，灰熊会袭击家畜、闯入庭院觅食；但只要人们清除院落营地的食物与诱物、给禽舍等加装电围栏，灰熊通常会无事经过，从而实现人熊共存。
paragraphs.function: 总结升华：指出采取预防措施即可与灰熊和平相处。

q-2023-jia-028.questionFocus: 考查谁为作者打开了哲学之门，即作者最初接触哲学的引路人。
q-2023-jia-028.stemTranslationZh: 是谁为作者打开了哲学之门？

trap.sourceQuote: Nothing kills the love for philosophy faster than people who think they understand Foucault, Baudrillard, or Confucius better than you—and then try to explain them.
trap.explanation: Foucault 只是原文中被提到的哲学家之一，与「为作者打开哲学之门」无关，对象错配。

trapEvidence.quote: people who think they understand Foucault, Baudrillard, or Confucius better than you
trapEvidence.anchor: Foucault 仅是被提及的哲学家

trap.sourceQuote: Eric Weiner’s The Socrates Express: In Search of Life Lessons from Dead Philosophers reawakened my love for philosophy.
trap.explanation: Eric Weiner 是「重新唤起」作者哲学热爱的人，而非最初「打开哲学之门」的人，对象与时间节点错配。

trapEvidence.anchor: Weiner 是重燃而非启蒙者

evidence.quote: an uncle gave me a copy of Jostein Gaarder’s Sophie’s World
evidence.anchor: 贾德的《苏菲的世界》

evidence.quote: It spoke to me and brought me into a world of philosophy (哲学) .
evidence.anchor: 把作者带入哲学世界

trap.claim: A college teacher opened the door to philosophy for the author.
trap.explanation: 原文未提及任何大学老师为作者引入哲学；大学时期反而是热爱被浇灭的阶段。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: opened the door to philosophy
locationParaphrases.targetText: It spoke to me and brought me into a world of philosophy (哲学) .
locationParaphrases.note: 题干 opened the door to philosophy（打开哲学之门）对应原文 brought me into a world of philosophy（把我带入哲学世界），而带来此书的正是 Jostein Gaarder 的《Sophie’s World》。

q-2023-jia-029.questionFocus: 考查第四段列举苏格拉底、梭罗等伟大哲学家的写作意图。
q-2023-jia-029.stemTranslationZh: 作者在第四段列举伟大的哲学家是为了什么？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了把韦纳与他们作比较。

trap.claim: The author lists the philosophers to compare Weiner with them.
trap.explanation: 第四段列举哲学家是为说明 Weiner 书中教读者学到的内容，并未将 Weiner 与这些哲学家作高下比较，原文未提及。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了举出伟大著作的例子。

trap.sourceQuote: we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche
trap.sourceHighlight: wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau
trap.optionText: To give examples of great works.
trap.explanation: 原文列举的是哲学家及其各自的长处（思考、观察、聆听、无悔），并非列举「伟大著作」，把人物例证偷换为著作例证，范围错位。

trapEvidence.quote: we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche
trapEvidence.anchor: 列举的是哲学家而非著作

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了称赞他们的写作技巧。

trap.claim: The author lists the philosophers to praise their writing skills.
trap.explanation: 原文是借这些哲学家说明读者能学到的本领，没有评价或称赞他们的写作技巧，无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了帮助读者理解韦纳的书。

evidence.quote: The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche.
evidence.anchor: 用哲学家举例说明读这本书的收获

evidence.quote: This, more than a book about understanding philosophy, is a book about learning to use philosophy to improve a life.
evidence.anchor: 帮助读者理解这本书的性质

locationParaphrases.sourceText: To help readers understand Weiner's book.
locationParaphrases.targetText: The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche.
locationParaphrases.note: 第四段以 the end result is a read（读这本书最终的收获）引出列举的哲学家，目的是具体说明 Weiner 书带给读者的体验，从而帮助读者理解这本书。

q-2023-jia-030.questionFocus: 考查作者欣赏《The Socrates Express》一书的哪一点。
q-2023-jia-030.stemTranslationZh: 作者喜欢《苏格拉底快车》这本书的哪一点？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它对历史的观点呈现得很好。

trap.claim: Its views on history are well-presented.
trap.explanation: 原文谈的是用哲学改善生活，从未涉及该书对历史的观点呈现，无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它的理念可以应用于日常生活。

evidence.quote: is a book about learning to use philosophy to improve a life
evidence.anchor: 学会用哲学改善生活

evidence.quote: He makes philosophical thought an appealing exercise that improves the quality of our experiences
evidence.anchor: 提升日常体验质量

trap.claim: It includes comments from readers.
trap.explanation: 原文只提到 Weiner 加入自己的诠释，并没有说书中收录读者评论，无中生有。

trap.sourceText: The invitation is clear: Weiner wants you to pick up a coffee or tea and sit down with this book.
trap.relationNote: 原文末段的 invitation / offer 指作者向读者发出阅读邀请，与「开放式结尾 open ending」无关，选项借「结尾段落」的话题制造词面联想误导。

trapEvidence.quote: The invitation is clear: Weiner wants you to pick up a coffee or tea and sit down with this book.
trapEvidence.anchor: 末段是阅读邀请而非开放结尾

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Its ideas can be applied to daily life.
locationParaphrases.targetText: is a book about learning to use philosophy to improve a life
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 ideas can be applied to daily life（理念可用于日常生活）是原文 use philosophy to improve a life（运用哲学改善生活）的同义替换。

q-2023-jia-031.questionFocus: 考查作者对 Weiner 这本书的总体看法/风格评价。
q-2023-jia-031.stemTranslationZh: 作者认为韦纳的书怎么样？

trap.sourceQuote: Weiner enters into conversation with some of the most important philosophers in history, and he becomes part of that crowd in the process by decoding (解读) their messages and adding his own interpretation.
trap.explanation: 原文说 Weiner 加入自己的诠释（adding his own interpretation），带有主观色彩，与「客观 objective」相反，态度颠倒。

trapEvidence.anchor: 加入主观诠释，并不客观

trap.claim: The book is daring and ambitious.
trap.explanation: 原文用 fun、sharp、humor、simplicity 等词形容该书，并未将其评价为大胆或有雄心，无中生有。

trap.sourceQuote: The Socrates Express is a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity and gradually pulls them in deeper thoughts on desire, loneliness, and aging.
trap.sourceHighlight: a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity
trap.explanation: 原文称该书 fun（有趣）且 apparent simplicity（看似简单、易读），与「严肃而难以理解 serious and hard to follow」完全相反，黑白颠倒。

trapEvidence.quote: a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity
trapEvidence.anchor: 有趣易读，并非严肃难懂

evidence.quote: he does so with plenty of humor
evidence.anchor: 充满幽默

evidence.quote: The Socrates Express is a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity
evidence.anchor: 看似简单、直白易读

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Humorous and straightforward.
locationParaphrases.targetText: he does so with plenty of humor
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 Humorous（幽默）对应原文 with plenty of humor；straightforward（直白）对应第六段 apparent simplicity（看似简单、直白易读）。

q-2023-jia-032.questionFocus: 考查对第一段美国人对灰熊态度的理解，即这种态度的特点。

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们在人们心中引发复杂的情感。

evidence.quote: occupy a conflicted corner of the American psyche—we revere (敬畏) them even as they give us frightening dreams
evidence.anchor: 既敬畏又恐惧的矛盾心理

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们应该被圈养在国家公园里。

trap.optionText: They should be kept in national parks.
trap.relationNote: 选项借用第一段出现过的 national park 制造干扰；原文只说游客涌入黄石公园希望见到灰熊，并未说灰熊应被圈养在国家公园里。

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们具有很高的科学价值。

trap.claim: 灰熊具有很高的科学价值
trap.explanation: 原文未提及灰熊的科学价值；第一段只描述美国人对灰熊既敬畏又恐惧的情感态度。

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们是美国文化的象征。

trap.sourceQuote: occupy a conflicted corner of the American psyche
trap.sourceHighlight: a conflicted corner of the American psyche
trap.optionText: They are a symbol of American culture.
trap.explanation: 原文只说灰熊在美国人心理中占据矛盾的一角，并未把它拔高为“美国文化的象征”；选项夸大了原文表述。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: How do Americans look at grizzlies
locationParaphrases.targetText: occupy a conflicted corner of the American psyche—we revere (敬畏) them even as they give us frightening dreams
locationParaphrases.note: 题干问 how Americans look at grizzlies（美国人如何看待灰熊），原文用 occupy a conflicted corner of the American psyche 及 revere…even as…frightening dreams 描述这种态度，定位答案句。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: cause mixed feelings
locationParaphrases.targetText: we revere (敬畏) them even as they give us frightening dreams
locationParaphrases.note: 正确选项 mixed feelings（复杂情感）对应原文 revere（敬畏）与 frightening dreams（令人害怕）并存的 conflicted（矛盾的）心理。

q-2023-jia-033.questionFocus: 考查对第三、四段灰熊种群增长原因的理解，即什么帮助了其数量回升。
q-2023-jia-033.stemTranslationZh: 是什么帮助了灰熊数量的增长？

trap.sourceQuote: after centuries of cruel and continuous hunting by settlers, 600 to 800 grizzlies remained on a mere 2 percent of their former range in the Northern Rockies
trap.sourceHighlight: cruel and continuous hunting by settlers
trap.explanation: 原文说定居者数百年残酷而持续的猎杀使灰熊数量锐减，定居者的行为是导致灰熊濒危的原因，而非帮助其数量增长，二者作用相反。

trapEvidence.quote: after centuries of cruel and continuous hunting by settlers, 600 to 800 grizzlies remained on a mere 2 percent of their former range in the Northern Rockies
trapEvidence.anchor: 定居者猎杀致使数量锐减

trap.relationNote: 选项借用第二段 expand their range 的同族表达 expansion of bears' range 制造干扰；范围扩张是种群恢复后的结果，而非促成数量增长的原因。

trapEvidence.quote: As grizzly bears expand their range into places where they haven’t been seen in a century or more
trapEvidence.anchor: 范围扩张是结果而非原因

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 自 1975 年起的法律保护。

evidence.quote: In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.
evidence.anchor: 1975 年被列入濒危物种法

evidence.quote: Today, there are about 2,000 or more grizzly bears in the U. S. Their recovery has been so successful
evidence.anchor: 如今数量恢复至两千多头

trap.relationNote: 选项借用第三段出现过的 Native Americans 制造干扰；原文只说欧洲人到来时灰熊与原住民共同生活，并未说原住民的支持帮助了灰熊数量增长。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: What has helped the increase of the grizzly population
locationParaphrases.targetText: In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.
locationParaphrases.note: 题干问什么帮助了灰熊数量的 increase（增长），原文转折点在 1975 年灰熊被 listed under the Endangered Species Act（列入濒危物种法），此后种群得以恢复，据此定位答案。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: The protection by law since 1975
locationParaphrases.targetText: In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.
locationParaphrases.note: 正确选项 protection by law since 1975（自 1975 年起的法律保护）对应原文 In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act（1975 年灰熊被列入濒危物种法）所提供的法律保护。

q-2023-jia-034.questionFocus: 考查对第四段细节的理解，即是什么阻止了鱼类与野生动物管理局给灰熊“摘牌”。
q-2023-jia-034.stemTranslationZh: 是什么阻止了美国鱼类与野生动物管理局将灰熊“摘牌”（撤销保护名录）？

evidence.quote: Both efforts were overturned due to lawsuits from conservation groups.
evidence.anchor: 保护组织的诉讼使两次努力被推翻

trap.sourceQuote: Their recovery has been so successful that the U. S. Fish and Wildlife Service has twice attempted to delist grizzlies
trap.sourceHighlight: recovery has been so successful that…attempted to delist
trap.explanation: 原文说灰熊恢复成功反而促使管理局试图“摘牌”，成功回归是“摘牌”尝试的原因，而非阻止“摘牌”的因素；选项把因果关系弄反了。

trapEvidence.quote: Their recovery has been so successful that the U. S. Fish and Wildlife Service has twice attempted to delist grizzlies
trapEvidence.anchor: 恢复成功导致试图摘牌

trap.claim: 是生物学家的呼声阻止了摘牌
trap.explanation: 原文未提及生物学家就摘牌发声；第四段明确说阻止摘牌的是保护组织提起的诉讼。

trap.claim: 是当地农民的主张阻止了摘牌
trap.explanation: 原文未提及农民就摘牌发声；阻止摘牌的是 conservation groups（保护组织）的诉讼，与农民无关。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: stopped the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service from delisting grizzlies
locationParaphrases.targetText: Both efforts were overturned due to lawsuits from conservation groups.
locationParaphrases.note: 题干问什么 stopped…from delisting（阻止摘牌），原文用 Both efforts were overturned due to lawsuits（两次努力都因诉讼被推翻）给出答案，定位到该句。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: The opposition of conservation groups
locationParaphrases.targetText: lawsuits from conservation groups
locationParaphrases.note: 正确选项 opposition of conservation groups（保护组织的反对）对应原文 lawsuits from conservation groups（保护组织提起的诉讼）这一具体反对行动。

q-2023-jia-035.questionFocus: 考查对最后一段的推断，即在采取预防措施的前提下人与灰熊关系如何。
q-2023-jia-035.stemTranslationZh: 从最后一段可以推断出什么？

trap.sourceQuote: If people remove food and attractants from their yards and campsites, grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble.
trap.optionText: Food should be provided for grizzlies.
trap.optionHighlight: Food should be provided for grizzlies
trap.explanation: 原文主张清除食物与诱物以免引来灰熊，与选项“为灰熊提供食物”正好相反。

trapEvidence.quote: If people remove food and attractants from their yards and campsites, grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble.

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 人们能够与灰熊和谐共处。

evidence.quote: If people remove food and attractants from their yards and campsites, grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble.
evidence.anchor: 清除诱物后灰熊会无事经过

evidence.quote: Our hope is to have a clean, attractant-free place where bears can pass through without learning bad habits
evidence.anchor: 营造无诱物环境实现人熊共存

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 应该为灰熊修建一条专门的通道。

trap.optionText: A special path should be built for grizzlies.
trap.relationNote: 选项把原文 bears can pass through（熊可以经过）曲解为修建 path（专门通道）；原文只是说在清洁无诱物的环境里熊会经过，并未主张修路。

trapEvidence.quote: where bears can pass through without learning bad habits
trapEvidence.anchor: 熊可经过而非修建通道

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 可以引入技术来保护灰熊。

trap.sourceQuote: Putting electric fencing around chicken houses and other farm animal quarters is also highly effective at getting grizzlies away.
trap.optionText: Technology can be introduced to protect grizzlies.
trap.optionHighlight: Technology can be introduced to protect grizzlies
trap.explanation: 原文提到电围栏只是用来把灰熊赶走、保护家畜，而非用技术“保护灰熊”；选项把一处具体做法过度泛化为引入技术保护灰熊，且对象与目的均被偷换。

trapEvidence.quote: Putting electric fencing around chicken houses and other farm animal quarters is also highly effective at getting grizzlies away.
trapEvidence.anchor: 电围栏是为赶走灰熊护畜

locationParaphrases.sourceText: What can be inferred from the last paragraph
locationParaphrases.targetText: If people remove food and attractants from their yards and campsites, grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble.
locationParaphrases.note: 题干要求 inferred from the last paragraph（从末段推断），原文用 If people remove…grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble 这一条件句给出推断依据。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: People can live in harmony with grizzlies
locationParaphrases.targetText: grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble
locationParaphrases.note: 正确选项 live in harmony with grizzlies（与灰熊和谐共处）对应原文 grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble（灰熊通常会无事经过）所体现的人熊共存状态。
